findings.evidence: The only declarations in the diagonalizable file after the definition are namespace terminators (lines 47–49), and the split-torus file likewise ends immediately after its composite definition; using either equivalence concretely therefore requires unfolding its construction.
findings.fix: Add `[simp]` application/inverse lemmas identifying standard monoid-algebra basis characters and, for the split form, finitely supported integer characters.
findings.issue: `geometricCharacterGroupEquiv` and the derived `splitTorusCharacterLatticeEquiv` at `SplitTorus/CharacterLattice.lean:34` expose opaque equivalences without lemmas describing their action or inverse on standard characters.

summary: The principal diagonalizable and split-torus equivalences lack characteristic application lemmas, so consumers must unfold their implementation to use them concretely.
